speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The reports were mainly against debt collection tactics aimed at pressuring debtors into payment by causing public embarrassment and inconvenience to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such tactics have attracted significant public attention and affected the public's sense of safety and security.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In 2019, a debt collector made multiple visits to a debtor's home and workplace within a month to collect a debt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On three occasions, he wore a traditional Chinese funeral outfit to the debtor's workplace, while carrying accessories, including a banner with the debtor's face, a funeral lantern and incense paper, and engaged in actions, such as shouting loudly, chanting, kneeling and blowing a whistle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: He refused to leave even when told that the debtor was not present.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On one such occasion, he even shouted at the debtor's colleague.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some Members might also recall that back in 2015, six debt collectors visited a debtor at a food stall in Funan Mall to collect a debt.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They unfurled a large banner stating that debt recovery was in process and proceeded to disrupt the stall's business, including harassing the staff and damaging the stall's equipment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Such debt collection conduct is unacceptable and causes unnecessary alarm to members of the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The debt collectors in both cases were successfully taken to task under existing legislation, such as the Protection from Harassment Act and the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, we need to ask ourselves, can we do more to prevent such problematic debt collection conduct from occurring in the first place?

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Debt collection is a legitimate economic activity that facilitates the fulfilment of financial obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In countries like the United States and Australia, legislative levers have been put in place to regulate the conduct of debt collectors and take action against problematic conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We seek to achieve two objectives through the introduction of the Debt Collection Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Today, businesses that carry out debt collection activities are not regulated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no legal definition for what constitutes a "debt collector", nor is there an enforceable legislative framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Without a regulatory framework, it is challenging to definitively assess the number of debt collection companies and debt collectors in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is partly due to the variety of corporate structures that debt collectors can use for their operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For example, some debt collectors exclusively collect debt on behalf of others, whereas others operate in-house as part of a parent business, such as debt collectors employed by licensed moneylenders, banks and financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is a wide spectrum of companies operating within Singapore's debt collection industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: At one end, there are debt collection companies which have consistently maintained high professional standards and pristine reputations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Some such companies service institutional clients, such as banks, which, in turn, hold them to similarly stringent and auditable requirements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: At the other end of the spectrum, however, there are debt collection companies that operate within less-established corporate structures and are willing to adopt a wider range of debt collection practices.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These companies mainly serve small-scale enterprises or individuals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Most of the companies that are featured in Police reports hail from this end of the spectrum, in part, due to their more aggressive debt collection practices and tendency to skirt around the boundaries of the law.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For this reading, I will refer to them subsequently as "already-regulated businesses".

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In order to reduce regulatory burden and costs for businesses, the licensing requirements for each type of entity will be calibrated based on the law and order risk posed by its debt collection activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In assessing the law and order risk, we considered indicators, such as the number of harassment reports made against such businesses over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clauses 6(1) and 7 to 13 set out a licensing regime for debt collection businesses which collect debt from a debtor either on behalf of another person; or where the businesses themselves had acquired the debt, for example, factoring companies that provide cash or financing to other companies in exchange for the debts owed to the companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clauses 17 to 21 set out an approval regime for the deployment of their debt collectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The business models of such entities lend themselves to higher law and order risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the licensing regime, a business must apply for and obtain a licence to carry out debt collection activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There is no restriction on the number of debt collection businesses for which a debt collector can work.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A debt collector can be granted multiple approvals to work for various debt collection businesses at any one point in time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: All debt collection businesses, including their key appointment holders and the debt collectors, will be screened by the Police and must be assessed to be fit and proper before they are granted a licence or an approval.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In assessing whether an individual is fit and proper, the Licensing Officer will take into consideration, among other things, prior offences committed by the individual that are relevant in determining the propensity of an individual to engage in problematic debt collection conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Generally, these could include offences involving harassment or violence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The severity of the offence and the length of time that has passed since the commission of the offence will also be considered.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Applicants who fail to meet the fit and proper criteria will not be allowed to carry on a debt collection business or carry out debt collection activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The fit and proper criteria will be set out in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police will also publish the criteria and requirements on their website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To deter debt collectors from engaging in problematic debt collection conduct and causing disamenities to members of the public, clauses 10 and 21 allow the Licensing Officer to impose conditions on licensed debt collection businesses and their approved debt collectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 45 allows the Minister to make regulations to guide the conduct and stipulate the duties and responsibilities of debt collection businesses and their debt collectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Regulations that we intend to introduce include: one, requiring debt collectors to verify that the person from whom they are attempting to collect debt is, indeed, the debtor; as well as, two, prohibiting debt collectors from continuing to collect debt from a debtor, if the debtor has informed the debt collection business or collector by any verifiable means that the debt is in dispute or that the debtor has initiated a process to settle the debt through other means, which could include mediation or Court proceedings.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We also intend to introduce regulations stating that a debt collector must not engage in certain conduct when carrying out debt collection activities, such as displaying or engaging in any behaviour that threatens the physical safety of the debtor or any other third parties like the debtor's family members, or affixing notices in relation to the debt on a property that does not belong to the debtor or at any public place.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: First, a debt collector brandishing his fist to the debtor or threatening physical harm to a debtor or his or her family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Second, sending text or social media messages to the debtor threatening physical harm to the debtor or his or her family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Third, pasting a notice with the debtor's identity information on the door of the debtor's neighbours.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Regulatory action can also be taken against the offender, including revocation or suspension of licence, or cancellation or suspension of approval under clauses 22, 24, 25 or 27.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Debt collection conduct involving the commission of criminal offences and which do not fall under the regulations will continue to be dealt with under existing legislation, such as the Protection from Harassment Act and the Penal Code.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Next, we will be class licensing already-regulated businesses, such as licensed moneylenders and banks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are assessed to pose lower law and order risk, compared to debt collection businesses that are not currently regulated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The list of regulated businesses is set out in Part 2 of the First Schedule.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Under the class licensing regime, an already-regulated business need not apply for or obtain an individual licence to carry out debt collection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: An individual who is employed by a class licensed debt collection business to collect debts will not need to be approved by the Licensing Officer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Businesses and individuals under the class licensing regime also need not be subject to screening by the Police to assess if they are fit and proper.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Notwithstanding the above, clause 22 allows the Licensing Officer to take regulatory action against individual class licensees, including disapplying a class licence, if the Licensing Officer finds that the class licensee has contravened any class licensing conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This serves as a safeguard against class-licensed businesses that may engage in errant debt collection conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Persons and entities, other than debt collection businesses and already-regulated businesses that collect debts owed to themselves that were not acquired from another party, will not fall within the scope of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Examples include individuals collecting personal loans owed to them, or retail companies with in-house credit control departments collecting debts owed to the company, and, for the avoidance of doubt, the conduct of such collections will still be governed by other laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Entities, whose activities have been assessed to pose minimal law and order risk, will be excluded from the scope of the Bill.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These entities are set out as excluded persons under Part 1 of the First Schedule.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: They are: one, individuals who conduct Court-administered debt collection activities, such as the Official Assignee or the Official Receiver; two, law practice entities and insolvency practitioners that are already regulated under the Legal Profession Act 1966 and the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act 2018, respectively; and three, entities which acquire a debt or debts through acquiring or merging with a business, other than a debt collection business, in a transaction that includes the transfers of accounts receivable, or through the seizure of accounts receivable under a security agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This list of excluded persons will be reviewed periodically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: If it is assessed that there is a need to regulate any of the excluded persons in the future, we will do so.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill also introduces other offences and penalties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 17 sets out offences for: one, individuals who act as debt collectors for debt collection businesses without approval; and two, individuals who act as debt collectors for entities carrying on already-regulated businesses where the entities are not class licensees or where the individuals are not employed by these entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Clause 18 sets out the offence for licensees who deploy individuals to act as debt collectors where such deployment has not been approved.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill provides powers for the Police to administer the regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These include: one, powers related to the administering of the licensing and approval regimes; two, powers of entry into premises used for a debt collection business or already-regulated business and other powers following such entry; three, powers of investigations, including powers to require relevant persons to provide information or attend before the Police; and four, powers to appoint non-public officers as compliance officers who will assist with inspections of regulated parties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: These powers are similar to those accorded to Police under other regulatory regimes, such as the Massage Establishments Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Bill allows persons, including applicants and licensees, to appeal to the Minister against an appealable decision made by the Licensing Officer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Appealable decisions include the refusal to grant or renew a licence and the refusal to grant an approval for an individual to be deployed as a debt collector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Minister's decision on an appeal is final.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Unless otherwise directed by the Minister, the decision appealed against must be complied with until the determination of the appeal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Lastly, the Bill provides saving and transitional provisions to ensure that sufficient time is provided for existing debt collection businesses and debt collectors who wish to continue operating their debt collection business or acting as debt collectors to transit into the new regime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: To conclude, this Bill seeks to introduce a regulatory framework to improve the conduct of the debt collection industry and better address disamenities that may arise from problematic debt collection conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In Mandarin):   Debt collection is a legitimate economic activity that facilitates the fulfilment of financial obligations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: However, debt collectors should not resort to extreme debt collection methods to collect debt from individuals or businesses, especially if these methods also affect the public's sense of safety and security.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Hence, to prevent disamenities to members of the public, we will regulate the debt collection industry, set standards for entry into the industry and impose appropriate licensing requirements on debt collection businesses and debt collectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is to prevent problematic debt collection conduct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Meanwhile, we will also put in place appropriate levers to take errant debt collection businesses and debt collectors to task.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: In order to reduce the regulatory burden and the costs for businesses, the licensing requirements for each type of debt collection entity will be calibrated based on the law and order risk posed by its debt collection activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, Sir, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But debt collection must be performed in a regulated and civil manner.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Licensing debt collecting companies is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to stamp out problematic debt collection activities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand that a range of offences under the Organised Crime Act, Vandalism Act and Protection from Harassment Act would be given more weight against the approval of licence.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would the Licensing Officer also take into consideration the age of the debt collector at the time of the offence, the frequency of the offences and the interval between the last offence and the time of licence application?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is not merely for the benefit of the licensed debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It also benefits potential victims of improper licensed debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There was a very recent case of a resident who started with legitimate intentions to get a $30,000 loan from a purportedly licensed moneylender.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, she ended up losing even more cash in a loan scam.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: She also got harassed by loan sharks and even got duped into being a money mule.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As such, having clear guidelines would help residents not fall prey to dubious debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Another area of concern is the coverage of communication channels.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Any messages that they send also have to be private.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are not allowed to post on the debtor's social media pages if it is public or visible to contacts.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to adopt similar rules here in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I also wish to ask how the Bill applies to the guarantors of debtors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I support the move to disallow debt collectors to collect money or attempt to contact persons who are not the direct debtors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, can the Minister clarify whether this is also extended to guarantors of the debtor?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are guarantors bound by law to repay the debts on behalf of the debtor?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some people may have involuntarily agreed to become guarantors without expecting to be responsible for the loan.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This could happen when the guarantor did not have full understanding of the implications or they did it out of friendship or family obligations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Does the Bill deem guarantors to also be debtors?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would the Ministry also consider enhanced penalties for debt collectors who harass family members or other persons?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clear guidelines have to be followed through with compliance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Clause 16 of the Bill mentions that the Licensing Officer sets out the code of practice.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How will this code of practice be determined and how will compliance be enforced?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should debt collectors be required to wear body cameras?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Do they also have to produce their licence to the targeted debtor before embarking on their debt collecting activities?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Thirdly, Mr Speaker, Sir, we also want to ensure that the guidelines and regulations are not too restrictive to the point of hampering legitimate debt collection work.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is some concern that under the new licensing, with a list of guidelines on what debt collectors cannot do, the pendulum may have swung to the other extreme.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In order to reduce the ambiguity of what constitutes improper debt collection, would the code of practice to be introduced via clause 16 of the Bill provide a list of best practices and guidelines with relevant explanatory notes on what debt collectors can or cannot do?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: In Australia, the relevant government and public agencies worked on a debt collection guideline for collectors and creditors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Its purpose is to assist creditors, collectors and debtors to understand their rights and obligations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is also to ensure that debt collection activity is consistent with consumer protection laws.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Do we intend to set out similar guidelines?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a debt collector is found to have breached the regulations, what are the avenues for victims to lodge a complaint?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should a specific hotline or body be created to address these complaints?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My concern is that the finite resources of the Police may be clogged up by such complaints, which are often less urgent.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What action will be taken against the collector?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How do we avoid situations where a recalcitrant debtor makes frivolous complaints to hamper the debt collector's job and avoid paying their debts?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would it be the Police or the Licensing Officer?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Fourthly, Mr Speaker, Sir, how are Licensing Officers selected?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Police and Licensing Officers have a significant role to play in enforcing the regulations of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Debt collectors are screened by the Police and debt collecting companies are licensed by Licensing Officers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Can the Ministry clarify whether Licensing Officers are recruited from the Police or would they belong to another department under the Ministry?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am concerned that some of these companies, especially those that are paid on a commission basis, may resort to hard-handed measures to collect debt, especially if it means that they earn more in return.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: More importantly, we should strive to solve the problem upstream by reducing the incidence of overdue debts.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This would require more public education about borrowing money from different types of sources, be they individuals or licensed moneylenders.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Companies in the business of providing loans should always impose credit checks before granting loans.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Debtors, too, are responsible for learning and practising good financial management.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is to ensure that they can repay their debts in a timely manner.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They should also be aware of their legal rights pertaining to overdue payments and debt collection laws.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we move Singapore forward, we absolutely cannot condone any individual or organisation to harass or harm someone even if it is done with the objective of fulfilling their job responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Credit is essential for the functioning of modern economies and the availability of credit can support growth, improve convenience and facilitate transactions on both the business and personal front.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The danger of that is, of course, the resultant implications when debt owed is not repaid when it comes due, whether through one's unwillingness or inability to pay.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In the earlier days of our nation's history, unlicensed moneylending activities and their intimidating and violent means of debt collection are perhaps much more prevalent.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While I confess that I have not witnessed such activities first-hand, I am sure we have all come across stories of physical violence and intimidation by unlicensed debt collectors, known colloquially as "Ah Longs", or seen first-hand the words "Owe Money, Pay Money" and the alleged debtor's name and contact details painted on the walls of our housing estates to name and shame these individuals.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I believe it is not in the interest of Singapore's debt collection agencies to be identified in the same vein, given how they could play a significant and professional role in the recovery of non-performing loans.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I am thus supportive of the introduction of this Bill to institute regulations to better manage the disamenities arising from such activities and I believe that there is a need to elevate our nation's stance towards debt collection and rehabilitation and hold these companies accountable for the conduct of their debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: With this as a guiding principle, I have three clarifications in relation to the enforcement of this proposed regulation.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, I wonder if the Minister can share any guidelines that will result in a debt collection infringing on the intended principles of preventing alarm and nuisance to the public and whether there are clearer regulations prescribing the methods which are deemed unacceptable for debt collection agencies.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For example, we would have seen videos showing men in uniform creating a ruckus outside a debtors' home or office.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Where such encounters can be an emotional one, it is all the more important we clearly demarcate the out-of-bounds (OB) markers to better help guide their actions towards a less socially disruptive manner, which then fulfils the objective of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: We should not let demeaning, disruptive and intimidating debt collection tactics take root in our society and our laws need to make clear that such tactics and behaviours are not acceptable.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Second, I note in section 8 of the Bill, in determining whether to grant a licence, the Licensing Officer may have regard to, and give any weight that the Licensing Officer considers appropriate to, any criteria and requirements that are prescribed, but may take into account any other matter or evidence that may be relevant.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Similarly, in section 20 of the Bill, there is also significant discretion in determining whether an individual is a "fit and proper" person to be deployed as a debt collector.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Will the Minister make clear what are some of the current criteria, requirements and weightage that are under consideration when this Bill is operationalised?

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: It is important that we provide regulatory clarity on this matter and ensure that individuals are not unfairly discriminated against, or perceive to be unfairly discriminated against, when seeking out employment in the debt collection industry, no different from any other regulated industry.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Even for the well-educated and well-informed, this may not be straightforward.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: If left unchecked, these charges could continue to snowball inadvertently.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: While the intent of the Bill is to regulate this industry, I cannot help but wonder if this is equally an opportunity for us to explore how the debt collection effort can further evolve to become one that operates on a more holistic philosophy, as opposed to a zero-sum game, where debt collectors win by forcing debtors to cough up monies to pay down their debt.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: This could be through empowering or even requiring debt collection agencies to provide their debtors with referrals to means of assistance focused on facilitating debt repayment arrangements.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: For example, Credit Counselling Singapore (CCS) has been a recognised organisation which works with The Association of Banks in helping the debt-distressed individuals manage their debt obligations.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: However, I understand that credit counselling and the creation of a debt management programme are voluntary and not mandatory programmes.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: In this case, education on how to manage debt and restructuring one's debt, where possible, can go a long way in preventing occurrences where debtors pay a seemingly infinite number of minimum payments that only service the interest charges.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I applaud MHA for proposing to institute upstream regulatory interventions to manage the disamenities from debt collection activities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also thank MHA for conducting a public consultation in June this year to gather public feedback in preparation for this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification relates to the qualifications of compliance officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The new section 4 provides for the appointment of compliance officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, they can enter premises and question individuals, similar to Police officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that compliance officers have some powers similar to those of Police officers, will they be required to follow rules similar to the procedural rules under the Police General Orders?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My second clarification relates to the protection of compliance officers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This means that they are not protected by sections of the Penal Code that set out offences for obstructing public servants in discharging their public functions, for omitting to assist a public servant and for threatening injury to a public servant.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This lack of protection is despite the fact that compliance officers do exert enforcement powers markedly similar to public servants, as I previously noted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, how will it ensure that compliance officers are protected to the same extent as public servants when exercising similar powers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My third and final clarification relates to the appointment of individuals as debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 20(2) allows the Licensing Officer to decline to allow an individual to be appointed a debt collector if the individual is not a "fit and proper person" to be deployed as a debt collector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 20(3) allows the Licensing Officer to consider any prescribed criteria and requirement.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Section 20(4) goes even further in allowing the Licensing Officer to take into account "any other matter or evidence that may be relevant".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister also share if the approval to be deployed as a debt collector will be time-limited and subject to renewal?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Sir, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am glad that with this Bill, more is being done to regulate the operation of debt collection businesses and the conduct of debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I support this Bill but I do wish to seek some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have also heard anecdotes of enforcement actions from my residents.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Sometimes, we wonder whether certain actions taken by certain debt collectors have crossed the line as far as harassment and intimidation are concerned.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I presume that such rules will be listed in the subsidiary legislation and they must, of course, clearly stipulate what acts are allowed and what are not allowed, so that proper debt collection efforts can be carried out with the personnel involved knowing what is allowed and that debtors are not being subject to harassment, intimidation or abusive or unreasonable acts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: These are arguably beyond what are stated in Annex B.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Next, Mr Speaker, I would also like to ask what are the Government's plans to educate the public and enable the public to understand the requirements of such regulations, in order that as many members of the public will be able to discern for themselves what acts are allowed and what are not allowed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Public awareness will also reduce the chances of unnecessary intimidation and harassment.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It may better enable the public to report meritorious cases of errant practices to the Licensing Officer so that proper action can be taken against the debt collection company and/or its staff under Part 4 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If there are no public education plans as yet, may I urge the Government to look into an appropriate public education campaign to educate the public?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Next, I would also like to ask that the Government make it clear in its rules and public education materials the contact details and procedure for referring complaints of any acts or conduct by a debt collector which fall afoul of the requirements of this Act or its subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would also like to ask the Minister what are the Government's plans to assist existing players to adjust to the new requirements and the new enforcement culture under the new regulation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Will the Government be giving them more time and, if necessary, any help they need in order to fulfil the new requirements?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Besides the conduct of debt collection activities, this Bill also serves to regulate the operation of debt collection businesses generally and sets up the regulatory framework for debt collection businesses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Having a proper regulatory framework for all debt collection businesses is good as it should help to ensure that the industry and personnel working in it work within a clear regulatory framework.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This, in turn, creates certainty and allows regulatory action if businesses or personnel involved fall afoul of the same and we see this in clauses 17 to 18, 22 to 28.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is the industry comprised mostly of small players or larger ones?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Does the Government anticipate a consolidation of the industry following the new regulatory framework?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Does the Government collect data on how many Singaporeans are affected by legal debt collection and/or enforcement activities at any one time or in the past two years?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope the definition of "fit and proper persons" has taken into consideration the current make-up of the industry's employees and its traditional and likely sources of recruitment.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The exact eligibility criteria are not yet spelt out in this Bill but will probably be done in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Nevertheless, I hope that it will not seek to exclude persons permanently or for long periods of time from the industry merely on account of past misdemeanours.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Equally, for those who are currently in the industry, instead of excluding them from future employment, could the Government consider a flexible plan to engage and provide training for these employees to ensure that they will be trained and prepared for future deployment in the industry?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My speech will focus on several suggestions to improve our debt collection and management regime.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I shall focus my speech on four major points.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, highlighting some risks associated with leaving debt collection activities to be regulated by private actors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Fourthly, ideas to strike a balance between inclusivity and encouraging robustness in the licensing regime regulating debt collection.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Apart from these major points, I would like to also briefly touch on a few wider social issues regarding debt.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Before I proceed, I declare my interest as the chairman of an international research consultancy that has undertaken work in the field of debt management and related fields.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: To begin with, I note that the Debt Collection Bill grants powers to public officers, who may issue various different codes of practice.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such public officers may then appoint private actors, known as compliance officers, who would enforce and apply these codes of practice when examining the conduct and licensing status of debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such compliance officers are empowered to grant and renew licences to debt collection firms and to conduct investigations on such debt collection companies.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This role would require sufficient training and familiarity with possibly multiple codes of conduct on the part of compliance officers.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: As such, neither the debt collector, nor the compliance officers who oversee them, are public officers with statutory powers, vis-à-vis the public.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Privatisation of this regulatory mechanism may hold potential complications for both the debt collectors and members of the public.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Given that debt collectors will have frequent touch points with members of the public, it is of importance that the powers, rights and identities of such debt collectors should be easily understood by the public.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, the public will face significant challenges in verifying whether such debt collectors are legitimate.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, members of the public may not know the multiple codes of practice that may be proposed which pertain to debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: An example of an existing Code of Practice is the Credit Collection Association of Singapore's Code of Conduct and Practice, and there may also be other new codes of practice which are proposed and implemented under subsidiary legislation by the Licensing Officers under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: As such, members of the public may struggle in the following three areas.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And thirdly, to find avenues of recourse or feedback pertaining to any potential abuses of power by debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It is for this reason that I propose the following.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would mirror the Bill's proposed requirement for compliance officers to carry "at all times" their identification card when examining the compliance of debt collection activities of regulated businesses.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would be consistent with current Government resources, such as the moneylender's directory, which serves to inform the public as to who the licensed moneylenders are, for example.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would bolster and strengthen the legitimacy of the debt collection industry by improving accountability.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would ensure certainty and help members of public to have a common, clear understanding of the powers which debt collectors are allowed to exercise.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, this ensures transparency and minimises potential abuse of power.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This legislation draws a clear distinction between legitimate debt collection and harassment or otherwise unlawful behaviour.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Fourthly, public education and awareness campaigns should be conducted among members of the public so as to educate them on what constitutes unacceptable debt collection behaviour by debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, in order to deter errant debt collectors, perhaps the Minister could consider a reporting hotline or a platform on a Government-created app, which could be set up to enable members of the public to report errant debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This would help to shift some of the burden of enforcement against errant debt collectors away from the compliance officers and licensing officers, and to directly empower members of the public to raise issues regarding errant debt collectors, without overburdening the general Police line.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I note that clause 8 of the draft Bill provides that the Licensing Officer can only grant a licence if the Licensing Officer is satisfied that the applicant is a fit and proper person to hold a licence, and clause 20 provides that the Licensing Officer can only grant approval for an individual to be a debt collector if they are satisfied that that individual is a fit and proper person.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, the concern is that this might prevent existing individual debt collectors who are exemplary in their current work performance, but who have had some past involvement with the criminal justice system in respect of non-violent offences or existing debt collection firms who are managed by individuals with such a background, from obtaining licences under the proposed regime.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For instance, in a CNA article, one debt collection company raised concerns that "the proposed law would put a lot of us out of business because most of these debt collectors are ex-inmates" and also because "both of our directors have a chequered history".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Of course, this does not mean that the granting of licences should be oblivious to a person's past record.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: But there are different types of past offences and it would seem fair that, for certain types of past offences, after a certain period of time, this should not count against the individual entering this debt collection profession.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such an approach is consistent with the spirit of unlocking the second prison, and my Parliamentary colleagues, Mr Louis Chua and Mr Dennis Tan, have also made similar arguments.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In terms of determining whether individuals are fit and proper people to be debt collectors, I suggest that companies be allowed to send in testimonials on behalf of their existing employees who might otherwise fail the approval process due to their previous convictions and that adequate resources and a proper process be put in place to hear such appeals.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, when considering whether an applicant for a licence is a fit and proper person, I would urge the Government to take into account factors, such as the company's record, years of experience and complaints record, in deciding whether or not to grant the licences.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: CCS facilitates a debt management programme to help suitable borrowers repay their loans in manageable instalments.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: However, for such debt management programmes provided by not-for-profits, not every borrower is eligible and credit counsellors are not obliged by statute to define, prescribe, apply or enforce any eligibility criteria.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I hope the Government can look into how such credit counselling and debt restructuring services can be made more widely available, as well as for the eligibility criteria for various debt repayment schemes or debt management programmes to be expanded.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I also want to suggest that the Government work with not-for-profits and researchers to collect data on the reasons for which individuals experience debt management issues, so that financial literacy programmes, like MoneySENSE, can be focused on addressing precisely those issues and common mistakes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I would also like to call for more attention in financial education programmes to be given on risky retail financial products, such as some kinds of cryptocurrency products, which, anecdotally, have attracted many young retail investors.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In exchange for accepting certain restrictions for one year, these borrowers will be free from their debt after that one year.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In view of these reference points, would the Government consider launching similar debt reduction programmes for low-income families, with the aim of enabling them to escape the poverty trap, perhaps tied to participation in financial literacy programmes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This could be part of the holistic support provided by the social care sector to the poor, which includes many chronically indebted persons.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 3.56 pm until 4.20 pm.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have trimmed my original speech – you may be happy to know, Sir.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Yes, because a number of questions that I originally intended to pose have already been asked, so, I only have two questions to pose to the hon Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The assumption for a debt collection agency when it is engaged by its client is that there is a genuine debt to be collected.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In most instances, it would be a relatively straightforward matter through an acknowledgement by the debtor or as a result of a judgment issued by the Court.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There are, however, occasions where the debts are disputed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I have come across cases involving people who dispute the debts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For example, they may claim they are victims of impersonation or that the goods and services received are not within the quality expected under the respective contracts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Alternatively, they may not dispute the debts in principle but raise issue with the quantum instead.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In practice, the debt collection companies usually ignore the protestations of the debtors and continue to insist that the debts should be paid purely on the strength of the instructions of their principals, in this case, their creditors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In my respectful view, there should be clear rules of engagement where there is a potential for debts to be disputed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We may have to weave in requirements, such as the debt collection companies being personally satisfied that the debt collection assignments are genuine, before proceeding with the engagement.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: What guidance will the Ministry provide to deal with such circumstances?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Will they be limited to collecting unsecured debts against principal debtors or guarantors or is it intended they may also be involved in the recovery of secured debts?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Can they, for example, exercise the creditors' rights of repossession of assets that are charged in favour of creditors or subject to hire purchase agreements?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: If so, what safeguards will be introduced to ensure that such activities are done strictly within the bounds of the law and having regard to debtors' rights?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: I would, first, like to commend how MHA has considered debt collection to be a legitimate activity that facilitates the fulfilment of financial obligations.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: The proposed regulatory framework, in my opinion, achieves a fair balance between stemming undesirable conduct and avoiding being overly burdensome for the debt collection industry.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: It is on this premise that I have some comments and clarifications.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: However, the group of businesses under the class licensing regime is a very large category with organisations which vary in terms of their sophistication and debt collection processes.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: This category includes banks or credit card companies at one end and moneylenders or the smaller outfits on the other.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Next, as part of the approval regime under clause 20 of this Bill, prospective debt collectors for licensed debt collection companies will have to undergo a fit and proper assessment by the Police.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: While criminal records are a relevant factor, it is also a vital information for the debarment tenure to be well-calibrated.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: This is so that it will be consistent with the principle that all ex-offenders deserve a second chance, as championed by Yellow Ribbon Singapore as well as Members in this House.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Referencing the security industry, I have engaged with my residents at the Meet-the People sessions, who were keen to be security officers but were repeatedly rejected by SPF in their application for a licence.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: If so, can the Minister be clear on the parameters of what turning over a new leaf means, that they can be reconsidered to work in such jobs?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Moving on, in recognising that debt collection is a legitimate activity, I am also cognisant that some debtors can make malicious or frivolous complaints against well-behaved debt collectors to frustrate the debt collection process.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: However, the truth of each complaint can only be established after investigation, which draws on Police resources and potentially allows the debtor to delay the fulfilment of his or her financial obligations.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: In this case, as the Minister of State has earlier mentioned, complaints against debt collection companies will also be taken into account in the measurement of their behaviour.

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, as communications and collection strategies shift to the digital realm, can the Minister explain if the Bill will regulate undesirable debt collection activities conducted on online platforms, such as through messaging or social media?

speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
text: What are other levers available to counter online harassment by debt collectors to ensure that such digital means will not be exploited as a regulatory gap for harassment of debtors?

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Part of their demand for money will be met by moneylenders in return for higher interest rates.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the Ministry has stated, debt collection is a legitimate activity and the borrower has legal obligations to meet the terms of the loan repayment.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When the debtor is unable to do so, ideally, both lenders and borrowers should discuss and renegotiate the schedule of repayment.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, not all attempts for revised arrangements will work out smoothly.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some borrowers avoid communicating with their creditors altogether or disappear.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Others even made false accusations of harassment against their creditors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: On the other hand, there are valid complaints, such as against increasingly strange, or some might say, creative methods used by the debt collectors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are invariably unpleasant, often disturbing and, sometimes, outright alarming.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They are a vulnerable segment and susceptible to marketing attempts by lenders keen to exploit their need for loans.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Sir, I welcome the new Bill to regulate debt collection activities in our country through a licensing system which empowers the Police to stop inappropriate debt collection practices.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some debtors, unable or unwilling to repay the borrowed money, refuse to contact their lenders.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They should discuss and negotiate to reschedule their debt repayments.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In order to recover the money, the debt collectors use all kinds of methods to collect the money.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But some collectors go overboard and take extreme measures, harassing the borrowers' families, neighbours, colleagues and so on, or cause members of the public to panic, which is unacceptable to us.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Recently, I heard that some lenders, after learning that some people are facing financial difficulties, obtain their bank account numbers and directly remitted sums of money to them and then try to collect the debts and charge very high interest.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In English): In conclusion, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Affected parties live in constant fear that the debt collectors may harm them and/or their loved ones.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Some dread returning home or even picking up the phone for fear that the debt collector is after them.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The stress and anxiety arising from debt collection activities have caused some of my residents to contemplate suicide.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: There were cases where the outstanding debt owed is grossly overstated, with no basis.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Beyond screening for records of previous offences, how will the Police evaluate the suitability of the applicants to engage in debt collection activities, before granting the licence?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The code of practice under the Bill is intended to cover the conduct, duties and responsibilities of licensees.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is a critical component of the Bill to enable clear lines to be drawn on what specific actions would constitute unlawful activities and provide clarity on previously grey areas surrounding conduct of debt collection.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, it would be useful to prescribe a clear set of lawful practices.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It should contain clear rules on what is and what is not allowable, in order to provide debt collectors with a clear framework within which to operate, as well as to educate debtors on their rights.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The training may also cover relevant rules around the Moneylenders Act and the Protection from Harassment Act.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: As part of the licensing programme, debt collectors should be required to pass a test on their understanding of the debt collection rules and regulations before being granted the licence.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will ensure that all parties involved are not only screened, but they are also adequately trained to understand and uphold the code of practice in carrying out their duties as debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: One such example is the Debt Respite Scheme, or Breathing Space, in the United Kingdom.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Under this scheme, debtors can access legal protection from their creditors and debt collectors for a specific duration of time to seek temporary relief from debt collection activities, including a provision to tend to mental health crisis.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will go some way towards giving struggling debtors breathing space to get their financial and mental state in order.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Debt Collection Bill, when implemented well, has the potential to professionalise debt collection.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: All borrowers should recognise that borrowing money is a huge responsibility.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: They are expected to repay in full and on time, according to agreed repayment terms.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: A loan is a legal obligation and the creditor has the right to take Court action to recover the debt.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is important that anyone considering a loan should fully understand their borrowing terms and the reasons for doing so.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Notwithstanding my requests for enhancements, I support the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the state of the debt collection industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, we are not able to definitively assess the number of debt collection companies and debt collectors in Singapore because, currently, we do not have a regulatory framework.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked if the Bill will regulate the collection of both secured and unsecured debts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, the collection of non-monetary assets, including those used to secure a debt, will not be regulated for now, as such activities have been assessed to pose minimal law and order risk.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nevertheless, the Police can still rely on existing legislation like the Penal Code or Protection from Harassment Act to take errant collectors of non-monetary assets to task.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Louis Ng, Mr Leon Perera and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the criteria used by the Licensing Officer to assess whether an applicant is fit and proper to be granted a licence to operate a debt collection business or approval to be deployed as a debt collector.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, the Licensing Officer will consider factors deemed relevant in assessing the applicant's propensity to engage in problematic debt collection conduct, such as past offences involving harassment or violence, as listed in the Second Schedule of the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Licensing Officer will also consider the severity of the offences and the length of time that has passed since the commission of the offence.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The considerations used to assess whether an individual is fit and proper to work as a debt collector are similar to those used for security officers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The approval to be deployed as a debt collector is not time-limited.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, the approval may be revoked or suspended should the Licensing Officer assess that the debt collector no longer meets the fit-and-proper criteria.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We appreciate Mr Leon Perera's suggestion to provide opportunities for ex-offenders who may wish to join the industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Licensing Officer will consider their circumstances on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked if there will be differentiation among the class licensees, based on their respective risk profiles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Given that class licensees are already regulated by other Government entities, they are assessed to pose lower law and order risk, compared to debt collection businesses that are not currently regulated.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As such, we assess that there is no need to further differentiate the class licences for now.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nevertheless, we will monitor the situation and recalibrate the class licensing framework if the need arises.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked if there would be rules of engagement when debts are in dispute, including dealing with instances of debt collectors collecting debts from victims whose identities have been misused by impersonators to borrow money.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: During my opening speech, I mentioned that we will be introducing regulations to guide the conduct of debt collection businesses and their debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The acceptable process for this will be prescribed in subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Debt collectors will also be required to ensure that there is a proper contract detailing the terms of appointment by the creditor, the debt to be recovered, the payment schedule and the debtor's identity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These will minimise potential disputes between the debtor and debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will also add that for instances of debt collectors collecting debts from victims whose identities have been misused by impersonators to borrow money, cheating by personation is punishable under section 419 of the Penal Code.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If such cases are reported, the Police will investigate the matter.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, the Police do not investigate civil disputes about the debt.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua asked if there will be clearer regulations proscribing unacceptable debt collection methods and Mr Derrick Goh, Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if problematic debt collection conduct on online platforms will be prohibited under the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, we will introduce the regulations prohibiting any behaviour that threatens the physical safety of the debtor or any other third parties, such as the debtor's family members.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This includes sending text or social media messages to the debtor, threatening physical harm to the debtor or his or her family.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Livestreaming of debt collection activities, in and of itself, is not an offence unless it crosses the threshold for other criminal offences, such as the Protection from Harassment Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked if we will be introducing any regulations on prohibited debt collection conduct other than the ones we have announced in the public consultation paper.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Leon Perera asked whether levers under various legislations could be unified and harmonised.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Today, legislation, such as the Penal Code and Protection from Harassment Act, apply to everyone.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Taking into account our observation of the debt collection activities, we are introducing additional levers that are more specific to the debt collection industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about issuing a code of practice and putting in place measures to ensure compliance with the code.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the potential avenues for members of the public to lodge complaints against errant debt collection activities.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Members of the public may lodge a Police report online via the i-Witness Portal or Police’s e-services website.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may also do so in person at a Neighbourhood Police Centre or Neighbourhood Police Post.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If immediate Police assistance is required, they should contact the Police at "999".

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Leon Perera and Mr Dennis Tan asked about educating the public on the regulations under the Debt Collection Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Information on the debt collection regulatory regime will be published on Police’s website.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked if the Government can conduct a public education campaign.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We thank the Member for the suggestion and we will study this.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Yip Hon Weng have voiced their concerns over debtors who make malicious or frivolous complaints against debt collectors to frustrate the debt collection process and asked if there will be safeguards against these debtors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As the Member rightly pointed out, furnishing false information to cause Police to act against debt collectors is punishable under section 182 of the Penal Code.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Police will investigate and take action against the debtor if an offence is disclosed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are also safeguards within the Bill to avoid penalising innocent debt collection businesses and debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the questions raised by Mr Yip Hon Weng on regulating the remuneration structure for debt collection businesses, the Bill allows the Minister to make such regulations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, we have assessed that there is no need to do so currently.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Ms Foo Mee Har suggested for the management and staff of debt collection businesses to undergo accredited training programmes covering the debt collection regulations and for debt collectors to pass a test before they are approved by Police to be debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about training for potential debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will require licensees to put in place measures, such as proper training, to ensure that their debt collectors understand and comply with the Debt Collection Bill and other written laws.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, the Police will not be administering tests for debt collectors.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the selection of licensing officers and Mr Louis Ng asked about the appointment and protection of compliance officers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Compliance officers will be suitably trained before they carry out their duties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Unlike licensing officers who are Police officers, compliance officers will not be authorised to detain or arrest any individual, to search any place or individual, or to seize any property.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There will be audit checks on compliance officers to ensure that they are proficient in carrying out their duties and these safeguards are similar to other regulatory regimes under the Police’s purview.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On Mr Louis Ng’s point on protecting compliance officers, they will be deemed to be a public servant for the purposes of the Penal Code and will receive the same protection as public officers when exercising powers under the Bill.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked how we will assist existing players to transit into the new regulatory regime.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, the Bill provides saving and transitional provisions to ensure that sufficient time is provided for existing debt collection businesses and debt collectors who wish to continue operating their debt collection business or acting as debt collectors to transit into the new regime.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Chua, Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Don Wee and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked a few questions which are beyond the scope of the Bill but have close nexus with debt collection.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, whether there will be guidelines to help residents not fall prey to scams, whether the community legal clinics are sufficient for residents to seek legal advice, whether there will be measures to protect vulnerable segments of the population from excessive borrowing and making debt counselling and restructuring more widely available, as well as whether we can consider introducing a scheme for debtors to seek temporary relief from debt collection activities, similar to the Debt Respite Scheme in the UK.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will pass this feedback to the relevant agencies to study separately.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On Mr Don Wee’s question regarding unlicensed moneylending syndicates that resort to depositing unsolicited amounts of money into the bank accounts of ex-borrowers and forcing them to make payments for the unsolicited loans, there have been such cases reported since 2011.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Police will continue to monitor them closely.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Once again, I thank Members for their strong support for the Bill.
